summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Latvian documents: four PMLP spreadsheets of first-time temporary residence permits (2023 to 2026 H1), fifteen PMLP tables of valid permits (PDF 2015-2020, spreadsheets 2021-2026) and the 2018 inquiry-committee slides. New rows are almost all from the permit tables: every non-zero investor cell by nationality (main applicants, family members and, in the PDFs, both together) for the company, property, bank and bonds routes, plus every cell of the total rows; all columns add up to their printed totals, and all 362 rows already taken from the permit tables were re-read with the same values. The slides add Security Police screening figures (two proposed indicators), a re-registration refusal count and three events.

observations.location: sheet "dati", row 5 ("ALŽĪRIJA"), column R ("IEGULDĪTĀJS KAPITĀLSABIEDRĪBĀ", galv.)
observations.quote: IEGULDĪTĀJS KAPITĀLSABIEDRĪBĀ | galv. | ALŽĪRIJA: 2
observations.notes: First-time temporary residence permits issued in 2023, reason "IEGULDĪTĀJS KAPITĀLSABIEDRĪBĀ" = investment in company share capital (art. 23(1) p. 28); main applicants (galv.); nationality DZA. Sheet lists every nationality with at least one permit; nationality cells add up to the "Visas valstis kopā" row in every investor column. Investor-in-company permits may include holders under rules other than the investor point; PMLP labels the column "investor in a company".

events.title: MP's amendment proposal for the company-investment route submitted to the Saeima
events.description: A proposal to the draft amendments to the Immigration Law, submitted to the Saeima on 18 Feb 2011, would have granted a five-year permit for investing at least LVL 25,000 in a company's share or equity capital (with at least LVL 20,000 in yearly taxes), or for investing in a company that invests at least LVL 100,000 in development projects in Latvia. Recorded in slides filed with a Saeima inquiry committee.
events.quote: vai iegulda tādu kapitālsabiedrību pamatkapitālā vai pašu kapitālā, kuras investē attīstības projektos Latvijā ne mazāk kā 100 000 latu

events.title: Saeima committee partly supports the company-investment proposal
events.description: At its 2 Mar 2011 meeting the Saeima Defence, Internal Affairs and Corruption Prevention Committee partly supported the proposal and adopted a two-tier company route: at least LVL 25,000 in a company with no more than 50 employees and turnover or balance sheet up to LVL 7 million paying at least LVL 20,000 in taxes a year, or LVL 100,000. This wording entered into force on 16 Jun 2011.
events.quote: tika daļēji atbalstīts un iekļauts komisijas atbalstītā priekšlikumā

events.title: Inquiry-committee slides point to criminal case over the 2011 investor-permit amendments
events.description: Slides filed with a Saeima inquiry committee (PDF created 18 Jan 2018) say that criminal case No. 16870000911 contains a wiretapped conversation, about a week before the 2 Mar 2011 committee vote, in which a witness said the amendments were meant to attract 500 to 1,000 small investors, bringing perhaps LVL 50 to 100 million more for a development project; the slides ask law enforcement to check whether the 2011 amendments were obtained through corruption. They also say the growth in permits in 2011-2014 outpaced the Security Police's capacity to check candidates and propose an annual cap on investor permits. The 500-1,000 investors and LVL 50-100 million are a witness's plan, not programme figures, and are kept here rather than as observations.
events.quote: Ar grozījumu Imigrācijas likumā palīdzību plānots piesaistīt no 500 līdz 1000 mazos investorus. Tas, apmēram, varētu dot vēl no 50 līdz 100 miljoniem latu.

new_indicators.definition: Number of applicants for whom a state security service recommended or requested refusal of the residence permit or citizenship, in the stated period. Not the number of refusals decided by the programme authority (see applications_rejected).
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-lva2 for the Latvian Security Police (38 foreigners in 2015).
